description: Replace the two subsystems pinakes MARKETS as differentiators and that the 2026-08-11 audit put squarely in the REPLACE column. **(1) The 'Datalog engine' is a 530-LOC naive-fixpoint evaluator over 10 hand-authored rules** — `materialize()` re-derives every rule's full extension each round (not semi-naive), has no negation (a SECOND evaluator, `evaluate_schema_violations`, exists for that), no stratification, and arity hard-capped at 2. Its own docs record **3 of the 10 temporal rules failing to terminate at corpus scale**. **Soufflé is already an emit target with an equivalence test** (`datalog/equivalence.py` diffs swipl vs souffle tuple sets), so this is *'run what you already generate'* rather than a port — and it fixes the non-termination. **(2) Entity resolution is O(k²)** — `merge.py:214` runs `difflib.SequenceMatcher` inside `(label, lang)` blocks, and the repo's own `schema/CLAUDE.md` records **~64M comparisons on one Lexibank ISO block**.

userStories.title: Run the Soufflé program you already emit
userStories.description: Execution moves to Soufflé; the Python evaluator stays as the CI fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: Materialization runs the emitted `.dl` through **Soufflé** (1,142★ UPL-1.0, 2026-07-13) and the existing `equivalence.py` test proves the tuple sets match.
The 3 documented non-terminating temporal rules TERMINATE, with runtime reported — that is this story's proof, not the tuple match.
`materialize.py` is KEPT as the offline fallback exactly as it is today, so a box without Soufflé still runs CI (the reversal path is the status quo).
Recursion and negation become expressible; the second evaluator (`evaluate_schema_violations`) is either folded in or its continued separate existence is justified in writing.
userStories.notes: The equivalence test already exists — that is what makes this cheap. Do not rewrite the emitter.

userStories.title: Adopt splink for entity resolution
userStories.description: Blocking + union-find + probabilistic scoring replaces the O(k²) scan.
acceptanceCriteria: **splink** (2,333★ MIT, UK Ministry of Justice, DuckDB-native — fits the existing DuckDB dependency) replaces `_link_by_fuzzy_name`'s pairwise `SequenceMatcher`.
The ~64M-comparison Lexibank case is re-run and the comparison count and wall-clock are reported before/after.

The domain-tuned thresholds are PRESERVED as splink comparison levels — `lexicon_reconcile.py` raises the fuzzy floor to 0.93 because *'German Empire→Roman Empire fuzzes 0.88'*, and that knowledge must not be lost in the migration.
The REMOTE OpenRefine reconciliation against `wikidata.reconci.link` is untouched — it is already adoption, not reinvention.
⚠️ Do NOT reach for `dedupe` despite its higher star count — verified **last pushed 2025-07-29**, over a year stale.
The offline cascade is kept behind the same interface for one release, so a bad match rate is revertible.
userStories.notes: The thresholds are the asset. Porting the mechanism and losing the tuning would be a net regression.
